utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Belinda Pidwell, Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Eugene O'Sullivan, Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you, Mr. Njegus. Before I invite Mr. Zecevic to continue his cross-examination, I remind you you're still on your oath. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Njegus. We'll pick up where we left off yesterday, discussing the bylaws enacted by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D64, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, you are aware that there were cases of unlawful conduct with seized property in the Ministry of the Interior. That was one of the problems the Ministry of Interior faced.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see this is an order dated 6 September 1992, and it relates precisely to this issue and the statement of reasons describes precisely what I have just said, that there have been cases of registered illegal conduct with confiscated property. And it is thereby ordered that seized property be treated in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs and other regulations, that proper records of seized property must be kept, that such property must be treated the same as securities and valuables, and that members of the MUP who failed to comply with this order will be subjected to criminal proceedings and prosecution. Do you remember this order?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it very well. Among other things, because, as you can see, there is a handwritten note in the top right corner which I made. It says: Kekic, to the register. I wrote that down, and I told one of my clerks to put this order in the appropriate file. I remember this order. I know that it was sent to all the organisational units on the ground, and I remember that more or less everyone began executing this order thereafter. I remember cases of failure to comply, and I remember that Mr. Stanisic had taken appropriate steps in several cases of failure to comply.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D00-2376, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Njegus, that after a while, instructions were also enacted about the keeping of deposits. This was endorsed by the Ministry of the Interior and was passed on to SJBs.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. These instructions were prepared by the administration for crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the document on the screen? This is a copy forwarded by the chief of the Doboj centre on 25 November to public security stations in the territory of the CSB Doboj. Can we see page 2, because this is it just the cover letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here on page 2 is the instruction on the keeping of deposits, and in November 1992, the CSB passes these instructions on to the SJBs in its area. Do you remember this instruction?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the substance, but I know for a fact that this was prepared by the crime administration, and I know it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Considering the statement of the witness, I would like to ask that this document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D321, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now show the witness 1D53.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This, sir, is an instruction on how to draft the annual progress report for the Ministry of the Interior. In this case, not actually a report for the year but for nine months because the ministry started operating in April. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not precisely. But I remember that Petar Vujicic, in his acting position, worked actively to promote this kind of work and analysis and information, and that he sought data and information about the operation of the ministry, to the extent possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 8, please. That's the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For you to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we zoom in on the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, this is the signature of Petar Vujicic whose administration was in charge of this work.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Doubtlessly, that's his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the witness 1D63, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Njegus, here we see a letter concerning a questionnaire on war crimes. We see that it's dated 19 July 1992, and it was created based on the conclusions adopted at the collegium meeting of the MUP in Belgrade on the 11th of July. This questionnaire had been sent to all the CSBs for further action. That means to be passed on to public security stations in their respective areas so that all war crimes may be recorded in the format dictated by this questionnaire. Do you remember this instruction and the questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember it specifically, but I know for a fact that after these meetings and a certain amount of insistence by the assistant minister Dobro Planojevic in his acting position and Goran Macar who, I believe, at the time was coordinator, these problems were very often discussed, and I know that on their part they exerted every effort to issue certain instructions to units on the ground and that they did that both orally and in writing, and this is one example.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Dobro Planojevic was chief of the administration for crime prevention and detection.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was called administration for crime prevention and detection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the MUP of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up P530.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Njegus, when you were talking to my learned friend yesterday and the day before yesterday, you were asked a number of questions concerning the powers of the under-secretary and the minister respectively with regard to signing documents. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now show you the law, and I need Articles 14 through 20, and that would be on page 2 and 3 in Serbian, and it could be, I suppose, page 3 and 4 in English. Articles 14. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure you know this, but for the record and for the purposes of these proceedings and for the sake of transparency and to explain your previous answers. Article 14 reads that the public security service shall be led by the under-secretary in the ministry who will be accountable to the minister. It's a fact, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a fact. If you take into account that this Law on Internal Affairs was earlier enacted by the Assembly of the Serbian People on the 1st of April, but most of the provisions were actually incorporated from the Law on Internal Affairs of the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, Mr. Njegus, isn't it, that the Ministry of the Interior consists of the public security service and the National Security Service as two branches of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And each of these two services, the public security service and the National Security Service, is headed by an under-secretary or assistant minister -- sorry, deputy minister, who is practically managing that service.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without a doubt. I tried to explain that a moment ago. The organisation of the service was the same in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and we practically took over that type of organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You are trying to say that in the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina, like in all the ministries of Internal Affairs throughout the former SFRY the ministry was divided into public security and national security, and each of these services was led by an under-secretary?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to the next page - that's page 3 - to show the witness Article 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Article 20 concerns the National Security Service, and it says: "An under-secretary shall be in charge of the National Security Service ..." That's what we discussed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Managing the Public Security Service or the National Security Service implies that an under-secretary has all the powers for that service?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Practically, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So from that point of view, the issue of the powers vested in Mr. Skipina and Mr. Kitso [as interpreted] and Mr. Cedo Kljajic, who was under-secretary for public security, are not in question.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they're not. But if you allow me to explain. The minister of the interior, more or less everywhere and that includes Bosnia and Herzegovina before the war, was usually a politician, not a career policeman, but the under-secretaries in the Ministry of the Interior were top-notch professionals, as they should be. They were before the war and they were in our republic as well, with the exception of Minister Stanisic who was really a professional more than a politician, so that may introduce an element of confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 7, line 22, may I just correct the name. It is not Kitso, it's Kijac, referring to Dragan Kijac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I believe you also discussed with Ms. Korner the meeting of the collegium held on 11 July 1992 in Belgrade and then another meeting of the 28th of August in Trebinje. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have just a few questions on the subject, and I believe that will be the conclusion of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown P427, item 8. Or perhaps 427.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if Ms. Korner has shown you this document, but in your evidence, you did mention it, and you said that after the meeting a report was created and submitted to the President of the Presidency and the prime minister of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this is the document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be. Or perhaps it was called a summary report. I can't remember that detail. But, again, you see the handwritten note referring to Petar Vujicic, where it says "delivered to."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean that Petar Vujicic wrote in his own hand delivered to the President of the Presidency and the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's his handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown page 5 of the Serbian version. I think that the page number is the same in English. I apologise, I still have to find the right passage in the English text. I think the page in the English version doesn't match. But I'll read it out. I'm interested in the second paragraph where it says: "It was pointed out that the priority of the National Security Service and the crime service was the uncovering of war crimes for the documentation." It says among others the filing of criminal reports and instances of war crimes if committed by Serbs are also documented. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This was an important matter at the time. And if I may comment, that's why I was surprised to read the indictment for Mr. Stanisic in which it said the opposite. Namely, that he ordered and instigated, encouraged, et cetera, the commitment of war crimes. I was surprised to read that. As you can see here, he stood for the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have just been informed that the page in English is page 3. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: By the way, thank you, Mr. Njegus.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D59.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document was shown to you during the examination-in-chief. It's dated 24 July 1992. It is signed for the minister of the interior by who?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please repeat the name of the person who signed.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already confirmed that this is the signature of Goran Macar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Who was deputy assistant minister -- deputy assistant minister Dobroje Planojevic for crime prevention; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I believe that you have already said this to Ms. Korner, but the OTP argues that, in this manner, by such orders, the perpetrators of crimes are, in fact, amnestied. It is the OTP case that people who act inappropriately as MUP members are taken off the register of the ministry and transferred to the army, in accordance with their war time assignments. It is a fact, however, that criminal accountability?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's -- I don't think A, that it's proper to put a question like that. It's the OTP case. He can put facts or ask questions. But in any event, I take issue with the sentence, if it was translated accurately. It is the OTP case that people who act inappropriately as MUP members are taken off the register of the ministry and transferred to the army. That is absolutely not our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will withdraw, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let us simplify. The issue of the criminal accountability of the perpetrator is regulated by the law, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the status of the perpetrator being either a member of the MUP or a civilian, if he or she commits a crime, the employees of the Ministry of the Interior are duty-bound to launch measures in accordance with their authority, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is clear. But if you allow, I can give -- provide a comment to what Mr. Macar signed. There was something of a debate between the OTP and me about this, and my impression is that they drew a wrong conclusion. The purpose of this order signed by Mr. Macar was the following. At that moment, due to the information that people were -- who shouldn't have did wear police uniforms, it was decided that the members of the reserve police force should be discharged from the police as soon as possible and put at the disposal of the army. But this is not -- does not mean amnesty for criminal or other accountability for their act, so they may still have to serve prison sentences. So this decision, or order, does not constitute an amnesty and does not mean that they are not -- will not be held accountable for the deeds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown document 65 ter 10371.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you that you spoke with Ms. Korner about this document, which is an authorisation for Danilo Vukovic, who was a crime investigator of the MUP, to visit and inspect some SJBs in the area of CSB Bijeljina. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said then that Danilo Vukovic not only carried out that task but investigated Dragan Andan who also accompanied him, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Basically these crime investigators of the MUP go to the territory of the CSB to learn about the circumstances there, find out the shortcomings, and facilitate the enhancement of the work of the SJBs, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I have already explained, we didn't have many people with ample experience in either the crime police or the uniformed police at the time. But where it was possible and where the circumstances allowed it, we did send out these investigators to the field to places where we had heard there were problems for them to be able to assist and file adequate reports that would make it possible to take measures. I know that Danilo Vukovic was sent to these towns, as well as Dragan Andan. Some others were sent to Herzegovina, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it, that when these investigators left to -- for their fact-finding mission, some paramilitary units were arrested. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That was one of the larger activities in the area of Zvornik against the paramilitary group that was called Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document if there is no objection against that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit 1D322, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D00-5174.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned a short while ago that some investigators of the ministry went to Herzegovina. Now that we spoke about Danilo Vukovic, you mentioned that some went to Herzegovina. Do you remember Vojin Vukovic, an investigator?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that he was sent there, possibly twice. I also remember Slavko Draskovic. He was also sent there, and I believe there was a third person with them, Milanovic, or some such. They were sent down there, and some of them twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know if you have seen this document. It's a document which the chief of the CSB, Krsto Savic sent to the minister and as far as I can tell, he is protesting and opposing the arrival of Investigator Vojin Vukovic, who, obviously had instructions to establish a police station with the SJB of the Gacko. And among others, in the last-but-one paragraph, he says that this investigator, although he was sent by the ministry, does not have the necessary respect and trust of the populus. And in the last paragraph, he requests more detailed information about the reasons for establishing a police station in Gacko. And he refers to a joint solution of the situation. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know the document. But I'm familiar with this problem and the incident that occurred in the relations between the then-chief of the CSB Savic and Investigator Vukovic. I wasn't the one who sent Vukovic to the field and gave him instructions. It was his supervisor. But I know that when he returned he was very angry and dissatisfied by the way he was received there, especially by Krsto Savic. He was prevented from entering the police station, and this report drafted by Savic confirms that. I, of course, cannot remember what the crux of the problem was, but I do remember that there was a problem. Vukovic was from that area and later on he was sent to the field to Herzegovina, but I don't think he went to Nevesinje and those police stations around there, but to -- rather to Trebinje and other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What it boils down to is that the chief of the CSB, Krsto Savic, doesn't want to obey orders and doesn't accept the decision of a certain administration of the ministry, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, well, approximately. My comment would be, although I hasten to add that I don't wish to say anything bad about anyone, but this man Krsto Savic was a peculiar person and later events confirm that, especially the way he ended up. So he had his own particular views of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said he didn't respect anybody.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I seek to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... is it necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It struck me that the connection between this document and the witness is rather tenuous. Indeed, the -- one of the -- I was not -- I didn't fully understand - let me put that way - the last set of questions that were put to this witness about this document that he was being -- here is a witness looking at a document that he was not the author on and asking to give his -- to read into it certain impressions and then added to that were certain comments about the character of the -- of the author. And taken all together I'm wondering how useful that is at the end of the day. So that is one of my reservations about exhibiting it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours would indulge me, I would try to explain as short as I can. Your Honours, the witness knows about the problem that -- that existed with the author of this document, namely, Mr. Krsto Savic, the chief of CSB of Trebinje. On this document, and the witness acknowledges he knows that for the fact, is that one of the inspectors was sent from the ministry to co-ordinate and help establish the -- the -- the station, the police station in Gacko, and the chief of the CSB didn't want to go along with that. And he's writing this document, and the witness, although he does not know about this document, he knows for the fact that that was the case, and he -- he knows for this problem between the inspector that was sent and the chief of the CSB. And I believe that -- that that is relevant in -- in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the -- so the relevance of the witness's testimony and recollection as to the problem that existed between Mr. Savic and his superiors stands independently of the document. Indeed, inasmuch as the document is foreign to him, it doesn't assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. It is ultimately for the Trial Chamber to decide, and ... I try my best to explain why I think that this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if it helps, we don't object to the admission of this document at all. I mean, I didn't say so. I thought it was obvious, but we don't object to it, and it's a document that may or may not have some relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zecevic, Ms. Korner having coming to your rescue and her last phrase may have some relevance, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And that is by majority that decision to admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D323, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P163.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a document you discussed with Ms. Korner. This is a summary from a working meeting of the leadership structures of MUP held on the 20th of August in 1992. Can you see the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Penultimate paragraph was the one you discussed with Ms. Korner related to arrest of 100 able-bodied Muslims. Do you remember discussing this yesterday at the beginning of the session with Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All this is actually the speech by the chief of CSB, Mr. Krsto Savic, in relation to the security situation in the Trebinje CSB area.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please look -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the previous page back in the Serbian version; page 4. E-court page 4, yes, thank you. The English text is where it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When this penultimate paragraph was read out to you in relation to arrest of the 100 able-bodied Muslims, I think that it was read to you without regard of the context because looking at the paragraph preceding it, according to which it is stated that an assessment of the Trebinje CSB, the security situation is threatened by about 300 persons of Muslim -- Muslims, armed Muslims who have rebelled who were organising into smaller groups, and then we have an explanation in the further text of the area where they are active. Based on that, one can draw a different conclusion. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. However, what we see written here most probably was stated and then transcribed exactly as we find here in the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As can you see, it's in the third paragraph. It says, after the block and the issues during which the members of the CSB stated main elements. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is stated here that the chief -- just let me wait for a moment until we've found the right paragraph in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it should be on the following page in the English version. Yes, can we please have the following page. One more, I'm afraid. I apologise. Yes, that's the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As you can see here, it is stated that chief of the Trebinje CSB, Krsto Savic, took the floor again and he is again complaining about -- or protesting about Vojin Vukovic and Dragan Andan and their behaviour. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The minister, in his reply, says that any objections from the field should be sent to the ministry for it to be considered and for possible measures to be then taken.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you've commented on the rest of it, I will have no further questions in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 153 document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That would be my last topic. I'll deal with you, Mr. Njegus. Yesterday, at the very beginning of my cross-examination, we discussed -- or maybe not at the very beginning but roughly at the beginning, we discussed the issue of the establishment of RS MUP starting from scratch. We said that there were about 40 and only 40 members of MUP in the headquarters, unlike the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina, where they had about 400 employees. This document, this is a list of salaries for May 1992, and if my calculations were right, one can see that there is about 39 or maybe 40 members of MUP. Can you please be shown page 2 of the document. According to you, according to your recollection, would this be a list of all MUP employees at the headquarters in May 1992? All together there's 40 of them.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is clearly so. There's no doubt about that. I can give you my comment in one sentence. You can see the number of people in the crime department police, how many people are there. Only four persons. Uniformed police only five. In my administration, just a few secretaries, and that's all. In the initial time, this is how the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit 1D324, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Njegus, thank you, I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I don't have any more questions for this witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Njegus. I am Dragan Krgovic. I'm representing Mr. Stojan Zupljanin, and I will put a few questions to you in relation to your testimony so far. Let me just follow up on a topic that Mr. Zecevic has discussed with you, and, of course, I would like to ask you to make a break after having heard my question, wait for a moment, because we are being interpreted. We don't want to have overlapping or problems with the transcript. And let me just state that we have never met before because you refused to have any discussions with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Responding to questions put to you by Mr. Zecevic in relation to transfer of reserve policemen from war time assignments within police to war time assignments with the army. And here's my question: A reserve policeman, upon receiving a war time assignment within MUP, that doesn't mean he is permanently employed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The reserve policeman is there on the war time assignment because immediate threat of war was proclaimed and should such an officer be responsible for a disciplinary violation, his removal from police war time assignment to some other assignment, war time assignment, either in the army or somewhere else, that process exactly represents the -- the disciplinary proceedings against him.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But that does not mean that his criminal accountability is abolished by doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In essence, the most severe penalty within disciplinary proceedings is termination of employment.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The very fact that a person is removed from the war time assignment, police war time assignment, means that the measure has been handed down. Formally maybe not; but, in essence, yes?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can make such a conclusion, yes. In essence, that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony, responding to the questions, both by the Prosecutor and Mr. Zecevic, you mentioned this meeting. And one of the problems that was discussed at the meeting was engagement of the police by the army in combat operations. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the early days, after the breakout of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina it would happen, wouldn't it, that police or the army, rather, would subordinate the entire force of a police station and send them to the front lines.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, all sorts of things were happening during this unfortunate conflict. Even situations that a paramilitary unit would take over the police station, steal all the weapons, documents, seals and so on. All sorts of things were happening, depending on the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court, P160. It's a summary from the meeting held on 11th of June or July 1992. Page 5 of the document in the Serbian version; page 8 in the English version. Page 5 in e-court -- or -- my apologies, no, it's rather page 8 because the e-court page numbers do not match the ones ... 03241855. Yes, that one. Fourth paragraph from the top, please. Starts with words: "Because of the losses in Mrkonjic Grad ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is what Stojan Zupljanin was saying at the meeting. He's discussing this very issue I mentioned a moment ago. Namely, that it is necessary to define the role of the police in their immediate involvement in combat operations. The army is asking engagement of the entire police force. They resubordinate them and then put them at the most difficult front lines. This should be stopped. Do you agree that such problems were present in the early stages of the war, as you've discussed it at the start with the Prosecutor, they didn't even ask for any kind of approval from CSB or the ministry.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course, I agree with you. Mr. Zupljanin was one of the smartest, wittiest chiefs that we had, and he had no problems saying openly what he meant. He obviously wasn't discussing this topic. These problems were present not only at the early stages but also throughout the entire war. Either with the army and even more with the paramilitaries. We have had different situations and problems where police found itself in an unenviable position. With time, the relationships with the army were improved; but, in the initial stages, it was rather disorganised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You also spoke of these problems in the relations with the army throughout the war. Now if you compare the forces of the police and the forces of the army from the viewpoint of combat assignments and the security situation, the Army of Republika Srpska had, at that time, between 250 and 300.000 members under arms.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figure. I know roughly how many police we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But from this report you drafted, we see the numbers of MUP personnel. It's a huge disproportion relative to the army. And the army was asking to have the police join combat activities, which had a great impact on the police force's ability to continue law enforcement.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to give you a picture. Many of them in the Army of Republika Srpska were practically jealous of the police, because the police force, compared to them, had more or less proper uniforms and equipment, and all the time they tried to push the police officers into first combat ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At the very outset of the war, when the MUP of Republika Srpska was established, was coupled with the outbreak of clashes and skirmishes throughout Republika Srpska and problems in the organisation of the MUP in the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, without a doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you said earlier in your evidence what kind of problems you faced on the local level, with various Crisis Staffs and municipal authorities. Now let me ask you a question from a professional point of view regarding the operation of the MUP and the role of various organisational units of the MUP. The work of the MUP of Republika Srpska was organised in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs and the rules on internal organisation of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The powers, the role, and the tasks of individual members and officials of the MUP were stipulated by the law, and they were working in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Every officer and official, as you explained to Mr. Zecevic, within the MUP and within CSBs and SJBs had their respective powers under the law and under the rules on staffing specifications.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It was not indispensable in day-to-day work in the management of the agency he was in charge of for him to ask instructions and authority from his superior.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only was it not necessary, it would even have been stupid. He was the primary person responsible for his area and for his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And speaking of organisational units, the basic organisational unit and the basic cell of the MUP, was the public security station, and it was accountable for the security situation in its own area.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the most important organisational unit on which everything in the territory of the municipality depended. And that is precisely where the greatest problems lay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the greatest problem, as you said, was with the inappropriate operation of these SJBs and their being in cahoots with local Crisis Staffs and municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really understand the question, but let me try to answer. As I said, the greatest problems occurred precisely on the lowest local level, such as SJBs. It depended on the particular municipality and the competence of the chief of the public security station. Chiefs were able or unable to deal with the problems. Of course, he could have been, at the same time, at the head of the Crisis Staff. To what extent a particular chief would be able to resist pressure from the Crisis Staff depended on his personality. It depended on his professionalism. So it all depended. It was different from municipality to municipality, but the greatest problems were faced precisely on the local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'll show you now a document, Exhibit P621. Tab 2 of the Zupljanin Defence binder. I think you've seen it before. It's a report of the Banja Luka CSB, progress report for the period 1st July to 30th September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The ERN number is 00749643. Start with paragraph 2. Could we enlarge the text, please. Paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think in your line of work you received this document. But Mr. Zupljanin discusses here precisely the problem you mentioned. He reports to the ministry that there occurred a functional and practical detachment of a certain number of SJBs from the centre, which considerably disrupted the unity and the social role of the organs and security services. And it also says that some of the SJBs attached themselves with -- to the local politics and leaders, neglecting their legal obligations and authorisations. But this occurred not only in Banja Luka. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen this during proofing, although I didn't read it back then. However, I'm sure that everything written here did happen in reality and happened often. I have no doubt about that. It -- it was simply a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, if this is a convenient point, it's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If you could you use the two minutes then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Njegus, look at the next paragraph. It says that almost regularly a number of SJBs turn a deaf ear to the requests and demands of the centre to inform them of certain matters, and they failed to react in good time to requests from the centre, which jeopardizes the unity of the organs and security services and their ability to act. In such circumstances, it is difficult to have a full grasp of the security situation, to make assessments, and make proper security evaluations on the territory of the region and the Republic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And we can only imagine how hard it was for Zupljanin to co-operate with certain chiefs in his own area, such as Simo, Drljaca, and some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you remember when you went on a field trip to Banja Luka, one of the problems discussed at that meeting was precisely the failure of certain lines of work in the centre to operate, precisely because of problems like this.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of your travel to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think now is really the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Njegus, let us continue with this. You basically answered all my questions about this document which we have in front of us. Answering the question of Mr. Zecevic, you spoke about the organisation of the headquarters of the MUP where there are two under-secretaries, one for state security and another for public security and what their powers are as compared to those of the minister. Was there something like that at the level of the CSB, where the chief had a -- of the centre had a chief of the sector of public security and chief of the sector of public security?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a regional organisation, and at the regional level there were the chiefs of centres of state security and chief of centres of public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And their powers were almost identical as at the level of the ministry, only they were at a lower level, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And within the public security sector there was also the uniformed police, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe only in Banja Luka was there a sector of uniformed police, and in the other centres they had departments instead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the chief? At the beginning it was Stevan Markovic in Banja Luka, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the late Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in the sector of the uniformed police for public security, they had under them the uniformed police and the special police forces, part of which was the special police detachment, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not quite. Part of the sector of the uniformed police -- or, rather, organisationally linked to them there were the police stations as well as the support units. That's the name that we had for them then. However, the special police detachments, as far as I know, had organisational links with the command at the level of the MUP headquarters. So they were not part of the centres of public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You are now referring to the period when the detachment was established at the level of the MUP of the Republic and the commander was Karisik?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I would like a clarification for the transcript. Answering the Prosecutor's question on page 11328 of the transcript of the 7th of June, lines 15 and 16, the language isn't quite clear. You spoke about Stojan Zupljanin and said that he was a good chief, to put it that way. And you went on to describe -- you went on to elaborate and said that he listened to all your instructions -- or, rather, he respected all your decisions and he obeyed all orders. As far as you know, orders from the MUP headquarters. And it was recorded in the transcript the other way around that he gave instructions to you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that case, it must be corrected, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I agree with you, may I say, Mr. Krgovic, when I read it. It doesn't make sense to me, but perhaps if we could have -- if you could read it out in English and then we can get what he actually wants to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll read out to you the English transcript: "He respected all of our decision. He provided us with all the necessary instruction. He gave us orders." This is the part I'm -- I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I remember, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So actually, it should be turned around. The answer was not recorded. Do you agree with what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. It must be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the functioning of the Banja Luka centre and Stojan Zupljanin, how you evaluated his work, you spoke from the point of view of the body that you headed. I will now show you Exhibit P625. It is a report on the activities of the MUP of the RS from April to December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Prosecution binder, it's tab 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So this is a report, a detailed activity report. I suppose that you were able to see it. And I would like to go to page 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbian version, it is marked F120-1298. It's the third paragraph from the top. It starts with the word [B/C/S spoken] in Serbian and in the English version it's the last but one. The highest number of criminal reports regarding general crime were filed by the public security stations from the CSB of Banja Luka 6.082 or 75 per cent of the total number. When you spoke about the efficiency of the centre you probably had in mind the -- this data. Namely, that most criminal reports were filed here more than elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Among other things, I probably meant this too. But I focussed more on the subject matter from my purview and for which I was responsible, and I've already said that we didn't have any problems with the Banja Luka centre. These are the regular statistics about police activities, and I'm sure that they faithfully reflect the situation in the territories of individual centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's turn to the following page of this document. The page reference is F120-1299.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And look at the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The English page doesn't match.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Two and a half thousand forensic analyses were conducted of mechanical and chemical traces, et cetera. Almost all of these activities, that is, 2.481 were carried out in the area of CSB Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's natural because our forensic centre was located in Banja Luka, so it is natural to expect that most of this was done there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Then there is the following paragraph. On-site investigations were carried out and anti-sabotage activities -- the -- and the percentage is 90 per cent of the overall number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let us turn to page F120-1301. I'm interested in the third paragraph from the top. It's about misdemeanour offences and reports relating to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Over 78 per cent of the 9.611 were filed by members of the CSB of Banja Luka; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if that is what the activity report says, then it must be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And basically when you were answering the Prosecutor's question and saying that you considered Stojan Zupljanin a police officer who had -- who was highly esteemed for his authority and integrity, you had in mind these results as well.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Among other things, that's what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Njegus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Njegus, let's stay with this document for a moment, shall we?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are we on page 20 in the English? I can't see ... No. Can we go to page 20 in the English. It is headed: Inspection tasks for protection from fire and explosions. I'm afraid I haven't the faintest idea of what it is in the Cyrillic B/C/S. Actually, it may be page 26. Possibly. It looks like there's a C there. Page 26 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I see, sorry, page 26 at the bottom, so whatever that is. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Does that -- is that a section headed: Inspection tasks for protection from fire and explosions?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is paragraph G in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That would explain it. Thank you. How's about page 20 in B/C/S. Is that a C? Anybody from the Defence want to tell me what page it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will. 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Krgovic. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I'm not clear, do I understand that you were involved in the preparation of this report, Mr. Njegus?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except, as I explained yesterday or the day before, I gave a contribution by submitting a personnel data. So in that part I was involved, but not in any other parts. This was mostly done in the analysis department by Mr. Petar Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware, Mr. Njegus, that during the period of 1992 in the areas which were taken over by the Serbian Republic, which were not already Serb, that there was massive destruction of mosques and Catholic church, churches, through explosions and fires?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, no. Unofficially, I did have such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. When you read this report then, were you surprised to see there's no reference in the section, inspection tasks for protection from fire and explosions to any destruction of any religious buildings?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Even today I can say, as possibly earlier, that this was a shortcoming. There was no reason not to mention these things, but it's a fact that there were no officially available data about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you say there was no reason for this. Would -- in your opinion, did this amount to a war crime?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. I cannot deny that. However, we didn't comment that. These days we even mentioned the daily bulletin of events which was made -- or rather, there were attempts by Mr. Vujicic to do that as well as possible, and he made efforts to learn such information from the field, and it did come in occasionally. But speaking about these matters, now I can say, that, as far as I remember, we didn't receive official information about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was this official policy that no documents prepared by MUP headquarters should mention the destruction of religious institutions?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can state that with full responsibility. None of the executives of the MUP in the headquarters did implement such an official policy. And you saw official documents in which we -- that contain serious warnings to that effect, and we always insisted on getting information from the field. There were criticisms for the failure to receive information, so I can repeat that there was no official policy of this kind on our part.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But if you knew unofficially and maybe common sense it was so widespread it couldn't be ignored that this was happening, did you, at any stage, make any inquiries or any of your subordinates directly to the chiefs of the CSBs, saying, We know this is happening. Can we have some reports, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I hope that you understand. This was not within my purview. But there's no reason for me to back out of this. The -- I know the colleagues who were in charge of the crime police, and I know from them that they requested their -- the organisational units in the field to give them objective information and to conduct on-site investigations and the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Specifically in relation to such crimes as the destruction of religious institutions?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember. We commented that, and, as far as I remember, they sent out such instructions to the organisational units in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you recall any discussions about this in any of the collegium, the big meetings you had in July or in August and September, in November?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, that issue was not raised, because, if it had been, it would have been mentioned in the minutes or summary -- that summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mico Stanisic travelled around the areas quite a lot, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, did he ever raise, to your knowledge, with you or the chiefs of the CSBs when they had meetings that something needed to be done to investigate and to prevent this destruction of non-Serb religious buildings?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You specified only this one segment, relating to war crimes. But as we have seen, he was, generally speaking, putting all his efforts and asking for the police work to be carried out to the full in relation to all issues. He did not have any discussions with me about it. Now, whether he did do that in relation to other people who are in charge of such issues --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to be fair with the witness, if the Prosecutor is talking about setting out explosives and creating general threats to the public, I believe that the witness should be shown the -- page 13 of the document, where this very specific topic is being discussed, something that's not being hidden from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so either he be asked once again, because he was referring to war crimes here, not all issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm now very confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... 36:14 -- 36:15.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, what do you want him to be asked again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the witness's answer was not recorded as was said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'll ask him the question again. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, my question was -- My question, sir, was: Did he ever raise to your knowledge with you or the chiefs of the CSBs when they had meetings that something needed to be done to investigate and prevent this destruction of non-Serb religious buildings? And your reply was: "You specified only this one segment relating to war crimes. As we have seen, he was generally speaking putting all his efforts asking for police work to be carried out to the full in relation to all issues. He did not have" -- sorry, it was an earlier part, wasn't it, you were ask about Mr. -- Sorry, which was the bit, Mr. Zecevic, you said that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that is correct what you were reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... okay. "Are to be carried out to the full in relation to all issues. We did not have any" -- he did not it should read, I imagine, not we -- "did not have any discussions with me about it. Now whether he did do that in relation to other people in charge of such issues" -- and then Mr. Krgovic interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now Mr. Zecevic says you said something else.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should probably now start from the beginning. With your permission, let me try and give you an answer in the following way. My memories, my impressions, the way I witnessed the period, I think I can say with clear conscience that in relation to Mico Stanisic that Mr. Mico Stanisic insisted on three or, rather, four issues: Discipline within the police force; work aimed at prevention and detection of crime; processing and removing from the police force those individuals who were involved in criminal activities; and for issues related to war crimes. I was a person active at the time. I wanted to be objective. I made a solemn declaration here. I don't have any specific reason why I would state things in any way that's different from what it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. The -- Mico Stanisic's four issues and then the issues related to war crimes. I want to understand your evidence. Are you saying that Mico Stanisic's insistence on the issue relating to war crimes was that all war crimes should be investigated?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whether committed against Serbs or against non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. During the proofing for this testimony of mine, you will remember I provided you with an example of such an approach by Mico Stanisic, in relation to Mr. Vlahovic, known as Batko.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly, which I reminded you. Your assertion is that it was Mr. Stanisic who ordered that he be arrested?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to my recollection of the events, that's how it was. I know this through Dobro Planojevic, who was at the time chief of the administration for criminal investigation police, who was ordered by Mico Stanisic, asking him to take all necessary measures to arrest a man because this person was committing war crimes in the area of Sarajevo, Lukavica, and so on, and I know that Dobro Planojevic did all he could, that eventually he was arrested by the military police, upon insistence of us from the MUP, and I also remember how soon he was again released, if that's of any importance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. And, indeed, he has only now just been re-arrested again recently, hasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, in Spain. And his extradition to Bosnia and Herzegovina is expected.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he was committing crimes against everybody, wasn't he, Serbs, non-Serbs alike?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was committing crimes mostly against members of the Bosniak ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I just to come back to, please, your assertions, please, about Mico Stanisic and investigations. You say that it was investigations into all war crimes, whether committed against Serbs or non-Serbs. That's -- that's what you're saying, is it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And whether or not Serbs were the perpetrators of the crimes or non-Serbs were the perpetrators of the crimes, the investigation would have been identically conducted?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, can we just look at the series of documents, please, that relate to this topic, because you were asked about this questionnaire. And so let's deal with that. Can we look, first of all, please, at 65 ter 127, which I believe is probably already an exhibit, but I can't remember what the number is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: P173. Thank you. Can we look at the last page of the B/C/S, please, to see the stamp and the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, it would appear, this is the genuine signature, is it, of Mico Stanisic, or is it somebody signing on his behalf?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is his authentic signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So this is an actual document signed by Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 16th of May, 1992 to the five security centres, to the chief, in view of the tasks resulting from the order by the minister of the interior ... of the previous day, purpose of monitoring combat operations and regular activities of the organs of the interior in order to collect documentation on the crimes against the Serbian population. Do you recall this order, Mr. Njegus?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember this. I did not take part in drafting of this. I would assume this was drafted by the crime investigation department or administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But this is clearly an order -- this is not something that was sent out without Mr. Stanisic's authority or knowledge or delegated authority, I should say, because he signed this himself, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He must have, since he signed it. But one should first take a look at the order because they're referring to this order here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You mean the one of the 15th of May?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But what I'm interested in, are you surprised at all to see, given you say that he took this overall view that all crimes should be investigated, that what he was asking for was documentation on the crimes against the Serbian population?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document before me is surprising to me because I know that general approach was treat all war crimes equally. And that's why I said that it may be useful to take a look at the order that's mentioned in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The 15th of May?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because maybe this is -- is what provides the general issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll check. I haven't actually got it here but we'll check as the witness has put it to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that document, and if you go on to the fourth section, which is page 3 in English, I think this was second page in ... so we see there is no misunderstanding about this. I think it is probably the second page in the B/C/S. Yup. Paragraph 4 or section 4, war crimes: "Measures and activities conducted to document war crimes. These activities must involve collection of information of documents on war crimes against the Serbs." So you would agree that there is no misunderstanding about what Mr. Stanisic is asking for here?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you. I must say that this document comes as a surprise to me. I don't know of this document, but I'm certain that this document does not amnesty other type of responsibility for war crimes against others.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But -- may not amnesty them, but it is not exactly him forcing -- forcing -- instructing the chiefs of the CSB to investigate crimes, war crimes against non-Serb, is it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true if one views this document out of the context, but if one remembers the conclusions from the meeting and some instructions that were issued, then I disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. The meeting simply talks about war crimes, I agree. But you have to look at that as a -- you keep saying in context, so we'll show you the order of the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 1D46. 15th of May, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. That's the order referred to in the document of the following day. I suppose we better go to the last page and see whether that's a personal signature or a facsimile. Now, can you tell us, Mr. Njegus, personal or facsimile?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Facsimile.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, clearly, maybe Ms. Korner could address again the previous document which -- which she stated that it was signed by Mr. Stanisic and it's clearly --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Quite different.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... I asked him. I asked him whether it was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But maybe you should readdress this because the facsimile and the signature on the previous document are quite different.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... well, you say -- I asked whether it was signed by Mr. Stanisic or was a facsimile. And I said it didn't look like a facsimile, and he said, no, it was signed by Mr. Stanisic. But I'm perfectly happy to go back to the signature. But can we just deal with this document, and I'll go back to the ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So this document doesn't talk about anything to do with investigation of war crimes or anything, does it? It's --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read it in detail. I expected one would find that in the document because the previous document was referring us to this document, and I expected to see a general position on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I mean, we can't give you the handwritten document. But if we -- it's on page 2 at the moment. Show you page 1. It's to do with the -- oh, no, I think we looked at this earlier, actually. Yeah, it was the war units one.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You're right. I expected to see an item here that would speak about war crimes in general, all of them, and that's why I asked for you to show me the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... well, let's go back, please, to the document I was asking you about, because you've been asked to have a look again at the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's P173. And we need the last page in B/C/S. All right. And can we highlight the signature. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I said that a moment ago and let me repeat it, I believe that this is a genuine signature by Mr. Stanisic. I cannot claim that with certainty, and it is different than the facsimile, but I think it is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you happy with that, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we move along, please, then. Can we have up, please, 65 ter 1232. There again I have a feeling that is already exhibited. P275. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, these are the minutes of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic, and I accept entirely, Mr. Njegus, you were not present at this meeting. But item number 3 is: "That the government draft a decision on the establishment of a state documentation centre which will gather all genuine documents on crimes committed against the Serbian People in this [sic] war." Now were you aware of the establishment of this documentation centre?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This was government policy, wasn't it, Mr. Njegus, translated into one of the organs of government - namely, the police - that was a priority was documenting crimes committed -- war crimes committed against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not up to me to make conclusions as to what is whose policy and whether it was so or not. But the other side had similar agencies and centres in charge of investigating crimes committed only against their people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can I assure you, Mr. Njegus, I'm sure you're right on this. But what I'm dealing with is your assertion that there was a policy of objective investigation amongst the Serbian MUP in Bosnia of investigating war crimes against all parties, Serbs and non-Serbs, and I'm just asking you on reflection and having seen these two document, whether you may be in error on that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I am. I still stand by what I have stated. However, I do understand that the priority was as what we've seen in these two documents, but I will stand by my claim that, in principle, in MUP of Republika Srpska, people who were in charge of investigating crimes tried to investigate all crimes equally. Now, whether that was implemented by others in the way it was intended, now, that's a different issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. As far as you're concerned, therefore, there can be no doubt at all, particularly from the chiefs of the CSBs and whatever, who attended the various meetings that they were supposed to be providing information to MUP headquarters via the CSBs on war crimes committed against all sides -- I mean -- Serbs and non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you were referred to that questionnaire, which I believe was then exhibited or the letter that sent out the questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, now -- we need to go into private session for this because it's a document under seal, P1072.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have up, please, P166.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is addressed to Mr. Vujicic. And is that -- is that your writing?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not. Most likely it isn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You have been able to -- you're saying no or yes because you have been able to identify your handwriting on other documents. Is that yours or isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. This is the July to September report from the CSB in Trebinje, addressed to the Crime Prevention Department and by this stage you are in Bijeljina or the MUP is in Bijeljina. If we go in English to the second page, and I think probably in B/C/S. Okay. So it's all on the first page, is it, in B/C/S? Or maybe the third -- could go on to the third page. Yup, thank you. Last paragraph. Apparently it says genocide somewhere, according to the translation: "Apart from the aforementioned, the CSB Trebinje ... submitted four criminal reports for war crimes against 138 persons in the case of killing a group of citizens of Serbian nationality in the area of Nevesinje and Mostar ... other inhumane acts and killing of civilians in Ustashas prisons in Mostar and Capljina and genocide against unknown perpetrators," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, can the Serbian version be lowered down or maybe next page because we can't see what [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
